To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

RXR alpha and RXR beta function as coregulators of retinoic, thyroid hormone, or vitamin D receptor-mediated transcriptional activation by forming heterodimers with the respective receptors, increasing their DNA binding and transcription activity.

RXRb is a coregulator that selectively enhances the binding of RAR to its cognate response elements and that RXRb also enhances the binding of the thyroid hormone and the vitamin D receptors to the cognate response elements.
RXR beta, a novel retinoic acid coregulator, enhances the transcriptional function of RAR, thyroid hormone receptor (TR), and vitamin D receptor (VDR) in a manner similar to that of RXR alpha.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of transcriptional control by the steroid/thyroid/retinoid hormone receptors and their heterodimerization partners, the retinoid X receptor subfamily.
the molecular biology of the retinoid X receptor, a ligand-activated transcription factor that is essential for normal embryonic development.
the identification and characterization of proteins that interact with the ligand-binding domains of nuclear hormone receptors and that are involved in the regulation of transcription.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RXR family is the coregulator of nuclear receptors.
retinoid receptors are the first coregulators to be identified and that RXR alpha, RXR beta, RXR gamma, and RXR delta are the first coreceptor family members to be identified.
RXRb is a coregulator for retinoic acid receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RXR beta is a coregulator that increases the binding of RAR to its response elements and also heterodimerization with the TR and VDR.
RXRb is a coregulator that selectively enhances binding of RAR, TR and VDR to their respective DNA response elements.
the RXRs are coregulators that enhance the binding of RAR, TR, and VDR to their cognate REs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RXRs have the capacity to enhance the DNA binding and transactivation of a variety of nuclear receptors.
RXRbeta can enhance the binding of RAR to retinoic acid receptors, thyroid hormone receptors and vitamin D receptors.
retinoic acid receptors (RARs) are regulated by a family of coregulators, the RXRs.
